label.ar: ▲ The 4 Core Digital SAT Commandments (نظام اختبار Digital SAT واستراتيجية الاختبار التكيّفي)

body.en:
1. 1. Always answer what is asked: The SAT frequently solves for \(2x\), \(x+y\), or \(b\), rather than \(x\). Highlight the target quantity.
  2. 2. Use regression for constant fitting: Type points into a Desmos table and use y1 ~ mx1 + b or y1 ~ a(x1-h)^2 + k to solve unknown parameters instantaneously.
  3. 3. Backsolve from the choices: On single-variable equations with complicated structures, substitute choice B or C to eliminate options rapidly.
  4. 4. Mind the reference sheet: Geometry formulas (spheres, cones, pyramids, special right triangles) are always available via the in-app reference icon — never guess a standard volume formula.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Digital SAT Format & Adaptive Testing Strategy)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Digital SAT Format & Adaptive Testing Strategy)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

body.en:
Problem: On the 44-question Digital SAT Math section, Algebra (~35%) and Advanced Math (~35%) comprise approximately 70% of the scored questions. How many total questions come from these two domains combined?

Solution: Multiply total questions by combined percentage: \[ 44 \times 0.70 = 30.8 \approx 31\text{ questions}. \] Approximately 31 of 44 questions test algebra and advanced math.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

The Digital SAT Math section allocates 70 minutes across two modules of equal length. If each module contains 22 questions, what is the exact average time available per question in seconds?
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

The Digital SAT Math section allocates 70 minutes across two modules of equal length. إذا كان each module contains 22 questions, what is the exact average time available per question in seconds?

solution.en:
Step 1: Calculate total seconds per module: \[ 35\text{ minutes} \times 60\text{ s/min} = 2100\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 2: Divide by the 22 questions in the module: \[ \frac{2100\text{ seconds}}{22\text{ questions}} = \frac{1050}{11} \approx 95.45\text{ seconds (about 1 min 35 s per question)}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Section-Adaptive Pacing & Question Formats

body.en: Module 1 contains a calibrated mix of easy, medium, and hard questions. Pacing and precision dictate whether you unlock the upper score bracket.

Module 1 contains a calibrated mix of easy, medium, and hard questions. Pacing and precision dictate whether you unlock the upper score bracket.

label.en: ⏱️ Digital SAT Math Pacing & Module Routing
label.ar: ⏱️ Digital SAT Math Pacing & Module Routing (نظام اختبار Digital SAT واستراتيجية الاختبار التكيّفي)

body.en:
The Digital SAT Math section consists of two 35-minute modules of 22 questions each (~95 seconds per question):

  • Module 1 (Routing): A broad mix of easy, medium, and hard questions. High accuracy here routes you to the harder Module 2, unlocking scores up to 800.
  • Module 2 (Scoring): Your difficulty tier is locked. Scoring well on the harder module ensures a top percentile score. If routed to the easier module, maximum scores are capped (~600).
  • Pacing Rule: Never spend more than 2 minutes on a single question in Module 1. Flag it, make an educated guess, and move forward to secure all straightforward points.

label.en: ⚠️ Digital SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Grid-Ins & Desmos Time Traps
label.ar: ⚠️ Digital SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Grid-Ins & Desmos Time Traps (نظام اختبار Digital SAT واستراتيجية الاختبار التكيّفي)

body.en:
• Over-calculating with Desmos: While Desmos is accessible throughout, entering complex equations for basic mental algebra burns valuable time. Use algebraic shortcuts when obvious.
  • Grid-In Formatting Errors: Student-Produced Responses accept up to 5 characters (including negative sign - and decimal . or fraction slash /). Never enter mixed numbers like 3 1/2 (read as 31/2); enter 7/2 or 3.5. Never round repeating decimals prematurely: 2/3 must be entered as 2/3, .6666, or .6667 (never .66 or .67).
  • Leaving Questions Blank: There is zero penalty for incorrect guesses. Always fill every single bubble or grid-in before the timer expires.
  • Calculator Angle Mode: For trigonometry questions, check whether the angle is given in degrees or radians. Desmos defaults to radians; switch to degree mode in the wrench settings when working with degree values.

body.en:
Problem: A student completes the first 16 questions of Module 1 in an average of 75 seconds per question. How many seconds per question remain on average for the final 6 questions?

Solution: Total time is \( 35 \times 60 = 2100 \) seconds. Time spent on first 16: \( 16 \times 75 = 1200 \) seconds. Remaining time: \( 2100 - 1200 = 900 \) seconds. Average time for remaining 6 questions: \[ \frac{900}{6} = 150\text{ seconds (2 min 30 s per question)}. \]
body.ar:

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

A student solves a linear equation and obtains the fraction \( x = -\frac{7}{4} \). What are the valid ways to enter this answer into the Digital SAT Student-Produced Response (SPR) grid?
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

A student حلs a linear equation and obtains the fraction \( x = -\frac{7}{4} \). What are the valid ways to enter this answer into the Digital SAT Student-Produced Response (SPR) grid?

solution.en:
The Digital SAT SPR allows up to 5 characters including negative signs and decimal points:

  • As a fraction: -7/4 (4 characters).
  • As a terminating decimal: -1.75 (5 characters).
  • Invalid: Mixed number -1 3/4 is read as -13/4 and will be graded incorrect.

Problem: Module 1 contains 22 questions, including 2 non-scored pretest/experimental questions. Psychometric analysis indicates that answering at least 15 of 20 operational questions correctly guarantees routing to the hard Module 2. Problem: A Student-Produced Response (SPR) question yields the exact fraction \( \frac{15}{42} \). How should this be entered in the 5-character Bluebook grid?

Solution: Reduce by dividing numerator and denominator by 3 to obtain \( \frac{5}{14} \) (4 characters: 5/14), or enter the 4-decimal-place truncation/rounding .3571 or 0.357. Reducing the fraction is always safest and fastest.

A student finishes the first 18 questions of Module 1 with 9 minutes remaining. Questions 19 and 20 are lengthy geometry proofs, while Questions 21 and 22 are quick Desmos system intersection problems. In what order should the student attack the remaining 4 questions, and why?
question.ar:
حل المسألة التالية في (Digital SAT Format & Adaptive Testing Strategy): Level 4 · Strategy

A student finishes the first 18 questions of Module 1 with 9 minutes remaining. Questions 19 and 20 are lengthy geometry proofs, while Questions 21 and 22 are quick Desmos system intersection problems. In what order should the student attack the remaining 4 questions, and why?

solution.en: Every Digital SAT question carries equal raw weight within a module. The student should immediately flag Questions 19–20, solve Questions 21–22 in under 90 seconds using Desmos, and spend the remaining 7.5 minutes on Questions 19–20 without time pressure.
solution.ar: Every Digital SAT question carries equal raw weight within a module. The student should immediately flag Questions 19–20, حل Questions 21–22 in under 90 seconds using Desmos, and spend the remaining 7.5 minutes on Questions 19–20 without time pressure.

question.en: If \( 2(x-6) = 3x-5 \), what is the value of \( x \)?

hints.en: Start from the relation: \(-x = -5 + 12\). Rearrange the terms in \(-x = -5 + 12\) to isolate \(x\).
hints.ar: انطلق من العلاقة الرياضية: \(-x = -5 + 12\). أعد ترتيب الحدود في \(-x = -5 + 12\) لعزل المتغير \(x\).

hints.en: Compute the value of \(x\) and check that it satisfies \(-x = -5 + 12\).
hints.ar: احسب قيمة \(x\) وتحقق من أنها تحقق المعادلة \(-x = -5 + 12\).
